lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Computing, Data & AI Check-In: Where Am I?
lesson.summary: A friendly tour of algorithms, loops, decisions, data, how AI learns and staying safe online, so we can see what you already know.
learning_objectives: Show what I know about algorithms, loops and decisions
Show what I know about reading tables and charts
Show what I know about how AI learns and staying safe online

blocks.markdown:
This is a **check-in** to see what you already know about computing, data and AI.

No computer is needed. Just your brain and a pencil.

blocks.alt: Code, data and AI: three big ideas in the digital world.
blocks.caption: Code, data and AI: three big ideas in the digital world.

blocks.markdown:
An **algorithm** is a precise list of steps. A **loop** repeats steps so you do not have to write them again.

Repeat 4 times (move forward, turn right) draws a square. **Debugging** means finding and fixing mistakes.

scenes.caption: Start with the robot at the corner.
Forward, turn right. Repeat 4 times to finish the square.
Back at the start. The loop made a square.

question.prompt: A robot does this 3 times: move 2 steps forward. How many steps does it move in total?

blocks.markdown: Programs make choices with **if** statements: **if** it is raining, **then** take an umbrella, **else** wear sunglasses.

scenes.caption: Else (if it is sunny), wear sunglasses.

question.prompt: If it is raining take an umbrella, else wear sunglasses. It is sunny. What do you take?

blocks.title: Debug the sandwich
instructions: Write the steps to make a jam sandwich, but put one step in the wrong place.
Swap with a grown-up. Can they find the bug?

blocks.markdown:
**Data** is facts we collect. We store it in **tables** (rows and columns) and show it in **charts**.

A **bar chart** makes comparing groups easy. Always check the labels.

blocks.title: A table: our favourite sports
blocks.caption: Each row is one sport. The number is how many votes.

blocks.title: A bar chart of the same data
blocks.caption: The tallest bar is the most popular. It is football.

question.prompt: A bar chart shows Cricket 8, Football 12, Swimming 5 votes. Which is most popular?

blocks.markdown:
Some programs do not follow fixed rules. They learn from many **examples**, called **training data**.

Show a computer thousands of cat and dog pictures and it learns to tell them apart.

If the examples are unfair or missing, the AI can make mistakes. So we always check what an AI tells us.

blocks.title: How an AI learns from examples

scenes.caption: We show the AI lots of pictures of cats and dogs.
It looks for patterns in the pictures.
Now it can guess: this is a cat!

question.prompt: An AI learns by looking at lots of examples.
question.hint: Think of the cats and dogs.

blocks.markdown:
A **strong password** is long and mixes words, numbers and symbols. Never share it.

Think before you click or post. Tell a trusted adult if something feels wrong.

blocks.alt: A strong password keeps your account locked, like a key.
blocks.caption: A strong password keeps your account locked, like a key.

blocks.prompt: Why might an AI that only saw pictures of golden retrievers get confused by a poodle?
blocks.answer_markdown: It has not seen any examples that look like a poodle, so it has nothing to compare with.

blocks.title: Copy the sequence
blocks.goal: Watch the order of the colours, then copy it.

points: An algorithm is a list of steps. Loops repeat steps.
Tables and bar charts help us compare data.
AI learns from training data, so the examples must be fair.
Keep your password strong and secret.

blocks.markdown: When you are ready, start the quiz. It has 15 questions and takes about 15 minutes. Do your best!

terms.meaning: A friendly game that shows us what you know. It is not a test.
A precise list of steps to do a job.
A way to repeat steps so you do not have to write them again.
Finding and fixing mistakes in a program.
A word that starts a choice in a program.
What the program does if the answer is yes.
What the program does if the answer is no.
Pictures that show data, like bar charts.
A chart with bars. A taller bar means a bigger number.
Pictures or facts that an AI looks at to learn.
The many examples an AI learns from.
A long password that mixes words, numbers and symbols.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for making toast in a sensible order.
questions.explanation: Bread goes in, lever down, wait, then butter.

items.text: Wait for it to pop up

questions.prompt: Repeat 5 times: clap twice. How many claps in total?
What does a loop do in a program?
IF the number is bigger than 10 say BIG, ELSE say SMALL. The number is 7. What does the program say?
questions.explanation: 7 is not bigger than 10, so the else part runs and says SMALL.

questions.hint: Think of the words from the lesson.
questions.explanation: A loop repeats steps and an if statement makes a choice.
questions.text: A {b1} repeats steps. An {b2} statement makes a choice.

questions.prompt: A robot should draw a square: forward, turn, forward, turn, forward, turn, forward. It draws a triangle. What is the bug?
questions.hint: Count the sides of a square.
questions.explanation: A square needs 4 sides and 4 turns, so something is missing.

options.text: It is missing the last turn or step

questions.prompt: Tap the one that is an algorithm.
questions.hint: It is a list of steps.
questions.explanation: A recipe is a list of steps, so it is an algorithm.

questions.prompt: In a table: Mon 3 cars, Tue 7 cars, Wed 5 cars. On which day were there most cars?
questions.explanation: 7 is the biggest number, which is Tuesday.

questions.prompt: Using that table (3, 7 and 5 cars), how many cars were counted in total?
Which chart is best for comparing how many students like each fruit?
questions.explanation: A bar chart makes it easy to compare groups.

questions.prompt: What can make an AI wrong or unfair? Pick all that apply.
questions.hint: Think about what it learns from.
questions.explanation: If its training examples are missing or unfair, the AI makes mistakes.

questions.prompt: An AI answer is always right, so we never need to check it.
questions.explanation: AI can be wrong, so we check what it says.

questions.prompt: A robot does this 4 times: move 3 steps forward. Slide to show how many steps in total.
Match each word to its meaning.
questions.hint: Think about what each one does.
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a list of steps, a loop repeats steps and debugging fixes mistakes.
A long password that mixes words, numbers and symbols is strong.
